newsitem.title: UK: British minister in bid to curb tv violence.
newsitem.headline: British minister in bid to curb tv violence.

text.p: A British government minister was meeting television chiefs on Tuesday in a bid to curb the amount of screen violence seen by young people.
Heritage Secretary Virginia Bottomley said she was concerned about the cumulative effect on young people of seeing violence on television, particularly in emotional soap operas.
Adultery, rape, murder and assault are portayed as part of everyday life in many popular British television dramas -- some of which are routinely watched by children.
"Repeatedly seeing people assaulting each other, using acts of violence, can't have no effect on young people. And of course it is very frightening for others," Bottomley told BBC radio.
"The overall evidence is that there has been a fall in the number of incidents...but the nature of those incidents is changing. Now there are much more emotional psycho dramas," she said.
Bottomley will meet the chairman of the BBC and members of the Independent Television Commission, which regulates Britain's commercial channels.

She said the V chip idea -- a device that allows parents to prevent their children watching certain programmes -- was still under consideration but needed more work. "I certainly wouldn't rule it out," she said.
